newsitem.title: USA: LTV sees $150 mln Q3 plant closing charge.
newsitem.headline: LTV sees $150 mln Q3 plant closing charge.

text.p: LTV Steel said Monday that it intends to permanently close its Pittsburgh coke and by-products plant by the end of 1997, resulting in a third quarter charge of approximately $150 million.
The company said it would have cost between $400 million and $500 million to correct the plant's operating and environmental problems, which was prohibitive.
LTV said the plant employs about 750 people. Two-thirds of them will be eligible for retirement, said the company, while the rest will be considered to fill vacancies at other LTV plants.

J. James Murray, general manager of raw materials and coke operations, said the plant has reached the end of its working life, with operating and environmental performance having deteriorated. He also said that on March 6, the Environmental Protection Agency issued a Notice of Violation for excessive stack and pushing emissions at Pittsburgh.

Murray added that "It would make no sense to perform major construction, which would involve the installation of new equipment and major rehabilitation, to put a temporary fix on the current operating and environmental problems."
LTV produces flat rolled steel and tubular steel products and is a major supplier to the transportation, appliance, electrical equipment and service center industries.
